nodes.name: Hydrothermal Vulcanization
nodes.procedure: A Ni₃S₂-based monolithic electrode (Ni₃S₂–NF) was prepared via in situ hydrothermal vulcanization on nickel foam (NF). The successful Ni₃S₂ growth on NF was evidenced by the electrode color variation, surface morphology change, and elemental/composition characterizations.
nodes.source_text: A Ni₃S₂-based monolithic electrode (Ni₃S₂–NF) was prepared via in situ hydrothermal vulcanization on nickel foam (NF).

nodes.description: OER LSV self-activation test in oxygen-saturated 0.1 M KOH electrolyte
nodes.source_text: 95% iR-compensated LSV profiles of the Ni₃S₂ electrocatalyst at different scans in oxygen-saturated 0.1 M KOH electrolyte... The potentials to reach an OER current density of 10 mA cm⁻² (E₁₀) for the first three LSV scans are 1.695, 1.659, and 1.656 V vs. reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE), respectively. The corresponding Tafel slopes... 162, 86.6, and 80.4 mV dec⁻¹... ECSA represented by the double-layer capacitance (C_dl) of 0.134 and 0.128 mF cm⁻²... surface area of 3.86 and 3.89 m² g⁻¹.

nodes.description: OER comparison with nickel oxides/hydroxides in 0.1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: LSV profiles of Ni₃S₂, Ni(OH)₂, Ni₂O₃, and NiO electrocatalysts.

nodes.description: OER LSV performance of Ni₃S₂-NF monolithic electrode in 1.0 M KOH
nodes.source_text: 95% iR-compensated LSV curves of Ni₃S₂-NF... in an oxygen-saturated 1.0 M KOH electrolyte. The E₁₀ and E₁₀₀... are 1.415 and 1.476 V vs. RHE, respectively.

nodes.description: EIS titration for charge transfer resistance analysis
nodes.source_text: electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) titration was performed at a series of potentials (from 1.54 to 1.70 V vs. RHE... At the titration potentials lower than 1.64 V vs. RHE, the lower charge transfer resistance (R_ct) obtained in the Ni₃S₂ electrocatalyst after the OER manifests the self-activating phenomenon.

nodes.description: OER stability test (chronoamperometry) at high current density
nodes.source_text: Chronoamperometric response of the Ni₃S₂-NF... excellent stability to afford a high current retention of 95.4% after 100 h OER.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM reveals core–shell structure with crystalline Ni₃S₂ core and amorphous 10 nm shell after OER.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscope (TEM) images of the Ni₃S₂ electrocatalyst after OER reveal an obvious core–shell structure (Fig. 2a, b and Fig. S14, S15, ESI†).

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM and EDS mapping identify oxygen-rich surface layer ~10 nm thick with S content 6.9 at%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: A distinct oxygen-rich layer with a thickness of ca. 10 nm can be identified on the surface of the Ni₃S₂ electrocatalyst... the sulfur element is also detectable in the outer shell region with a content of 6.9 at% (Fig. 2c,d).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mapping and linear scan confirm Ni, O, and S coexistence in outer shell (6.9 at% S) and only Ni and S in inner core.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Most importantly, the sulfur element is also detectable in the outer shell region with a content of 6.9 at% (Fig. 2d) to validate the assumption for forming oxysulfide species.

Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy map for Sulfur

nodes.characterization_summary: Surface shows O (m/z=16) and S (m/z=32) signals; after etching S strengthens and O disappears confirming core-shell structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For the mass spectrometry on the surface, signals corresponding to oxygen (m/z := 16) and sulfur (m/z = 32) can be identified... after depth etching, the intensity of sulfur signal strengthens while the oxygen signal disappears.

nodes.characterization_summary: Depth-profiling: surface O 49.8 at%, S 6.1 at%; Ni LMM peak shifts 1.0 eV left post-OER indicating more positive Ni charge.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The oxygen content decreases from 49.8 at% to about zero... while the sulfur content increases from 6.1 to 23.2 at%... the peak of the Ni₃S₂ electrocatalyst after OER is 1.0 eV left-shifted.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p blue-shifts 1.7 eV post-OER indicating higher Ni oxidation state; S signals persist after 1h, 10h, 100h OER.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XPS results reveal an obvious blue-shifting tendency of 1.7 eV in the nickel 2p spectrum after OER... all the samples exhibit obvious sulfur element signals based on comprehensive surface characterizations including... XPS (Fig. 4b).

nodes.characterization_summary: XANES Ni L₂,₃ edges peak intensities increase after OER, revealing decreased 3d electron density of Ni.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Based on the soft XANES measurements, the peak intensities of the Ni L₂,₃ edges significantly increase after the OER, revealing a decreased 3d electron density.

nodes.characterization_summary: No peaks of nickel oxide/hydroxide identified in XRD patterns after OER.
nodes.evidence_snippet: However, no peaks of nickel oxide/hydroxide can be identified in the X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns of the Ni₃S₂ electrocatalyst after the OER (Fig. S8, ESI†).

nodes.characterization_summary: Nitrogen isotherms show similar surface areas: 3.86 m²/g before, 3.89 m²/g after 1.0 h OER.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ni₃S₂ electrocatalyst before and after the OER also demonstrates a similar surface area of 3.86 and 3.89 m² g⁻¹ and pore structure based on the nitrogen adsorption/desorption isotherms (Fig. 1d).

nodes.characterization_summary: Double-layer capacitance C_dl = 0.134 mF/cm² before OER, 0.128 mF/cm² after, showing similar ECSA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: almost the same electrochemical surface area (ECSA) represented by the double-layer capacitance (C_dl) of 0.134 and 0.128 mF cm⁻², respectively (Fig. 1e).
